tips.title: Assembling Multi-Part Gun Barrels (Trumpeter, AFV Club)
tips.text: For multi-part gun barrels like Trumpeter's 1/35 M1A2 SEP or AFV Club's 1/48 Tiger I, dry-fit parts first. Apply Tamiya Extra Thin Cement to one end of the inner barrel, join it with the next part, and hold them together with tweezers. Let it cure for 30 seconds. Repeat this for all sections. Before applying paint, use a brass rod to gently align and strengthen the barrel.

tips.title: Jig for Wing Alignment with Eduard Alignment Pegs
tips.text: For wings that need to be perfectly aligned, use Eduard Alignment Pegs. Drill small holes in the wing roots, insert the pegs, and close the fuselage halves. Tighten the pegs to apply pressure, ensuring the wings are flush. Leave the assembly clamped until the glue sets. Remove pegs, sand any marks, and proceed with painting.

tips.title: Installing Eduard Photo-Etch Parts with Super Glue
tips.text: Before applying Super Glue to Eduard photo-etch parts, bend them using a GodHand nipper's flat side. Apply a small amount of Super Glue to the back of the part, let it capillary action for 5 seconds, then attach it to the model. Hold gently with tweezers for 30 seconds. Once set, use a toothpick dipped in acetone to remove any excess glue.

tips.title: Working with Resin Conversion Kits (Clear Prop Models)
tips.text: For resin kits like Clear Prop Models' 1/48 F-16C Vipers, clean parts with soap and water, then wash with isopropyl alcohol. Dry-fit parts to ensure a good fit. Use CA glue to attach parts, applying a drop to both mating surfaces. Join parts quickly and clamp them until set. After painting, use Vallejo Plastic Putty to fill any gaps, sand, and prime.

tips.title: Assembling Tracks: Individual Link vs Vinyl vs Workable
tips.text: For tracks, consider individual link (Meng 1/35 M113), vinyl (Arma Hobby 1/35 T-34/85), or workable (ICM 1/35 T-72B). For individual links, use tweezers to dip each link in Tamiya Extra Thin Cement, attach it to the track, and hold briefly. For vinyl, soak the track in warm water until flexible, then attach to the model using liquid cement. For workable, bend and attach directly to the model.
